items.note: A bit formal. Friends often just say the person's name or 早晨.
Answering the phone it is usually wai2.

items.en: thanks (for a service or favour); excuse me; please
items.note: Use for help or service: someone passes you something or holds a door, or when you ask for something.

items.en: thank you (for a gift or a compliment)
items.note: Use when you receive a gift or praise.
Goes before a verb or adjective.
Cantonese never says 唔有. 冇 is the negative of 有.
十一 = 11, 二十 = 20, 二十一 = 21. In speech 二十 often becomes 廿 jaa6 (廿一 = 21).
萬 is a unit of its own: 一萬 = 10,000.
Use 兩 before a measure word (兩個人, two people). Use 二 when counting and inside numbers (十二, 二十).

items.en: measure word for people and many things

hai2.title: 喺 hai2: at, in
hai2.explain: 喺 marks where something is or happens: 我喺屋企 "I'm at home". Don't mix it up with 係 hai6 "to be". Only the tone differs.

ge3.title: 嘅 ge3: 's, of
ge3.explain: 嘅 links an owner or a description to a noun: 我嘅 "my", 好食嘅嘢 "tasty stuff".

zo2.title: 咗 zo2: done
zo2.explain: After a verb, 咗 shows the action has happened: 我食咗飯 "I've eaten".

gan2.title: 緊 gan2: -ing
gan2.explain: After a verb, 緊 shows the action is in progress: 我食緊飯 "I'm eating".

gwo3.title: 過 gwo3: ever
gwo3.explain: After a verb, 過 means "have done before": 我去過 "I've been (there)".

mei6.title: 未 mei6: not yet
mei6.explain: 未 means "not yet". 食咗飯未呀? "Have you eaten yet?" is answered 未 or 食咗.

mou5v.title: 冇 + verb: didn't
mou5v.explain: 冇 before a verb means "didn't": 我冇去 "I didn't go".

anota.title: A唔A questions
anota.explain: Say the verb, then 唔, then the verb again to ask yes or no: 去唔去? "going or not?". For 有 the form is 有冇.

haimai.title: 係咪 hai6 mai6: is it that…?
haimai.explain: 係咪 is a short form of 係唔係 and asks for confirmation: 你係咪學生?

qwords.title: Question words
qwords.explain: 咩 me1 or 乜嘢 mat1 je5 "what", 邊個 bin1 go3 "who", 邊度 bin1 dou6 "where", 點解 dim2 gaai2 "why", 幾時 gei2 si4 "when", 幾多 gei2 do1 "how many", 點 dim2 "how". The question word stays where the answer would go.

gwo3cmp.title: X + adjective + 過 + Y
gwo3cmp.explain: To compare, put 過 after the adjective: 佢高過我 "he's taller than me".

bei2.title: 畀 bei2: give
bei2.explain: When giving, the thing comes before the person: 畀本書我 "give me the book".

dirs.title: 嚟 去 返: come, go, go back
dirs.explain: 嚟 lai4 "come" (also heard as lei4), 去 heoi3 "go", 返 faan1 "go back (somewhere you belong)": 返屋企 "go home", 返工 "go to work".

zyu6.title: 住 zyu6: keep -ing
zyu6.explain: After a verb, 住 marks a continuing state: 等住 "wait (and keep waiting)", 坐住 "sitting".

haa5.title: 吓 haa5: a bit
haa5.explain: After a verb, 吓 means "a little, have a go": 試吓 "give it a try".

maai4.title: 埋 maai4: too, finish off
maai4.explain: After a verb, 埋 means "as well" or "finish the rest": 等埋我 "wait for me too", 食埋佢 "finish it off".

faan1asp.title: 返 faan1: again, back
faan1asp.explain: After a verb, 返 means doing it again or getting back to it: 瞓返覺 "go back to sleep".

laa3.title: 喇 laa3: now, already
laa3.explain: 喇 marks a new situation: 夠喇 "that's enough now". People often write 啦 for it too.

wo3.title: 喎 wo3 / wo5
wo3.explain: wo3 shows you've just noticed something: 落雨喎 "oh, it's raining". wo5 reports what someone else said.

lo1.title: 囉 lo1: obviously
lo1.explain: 囉 says "that's how it is, obviously": 噉咪得囉 "then that's fine, isn't it".

me1.title: 咩 me1: really?
me1.explain: At the end of a question, 咩 shows surprise or doubt: 真係咩? "really?".

ge3fin.title: 嘅 ge3 at the end
ge3fin.explain: 嘅 at the end of a sentence says "this is so": 佢唔會嚟嘅 "he won't come".
